records.source: Διαμαρτύρομαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ, τοῦ μέλλοντος κρίνειν ζῶντας καὶ νεκρούς, καὶ τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: I solemnly charge [you] before God and Christ Jesus, the [one] about to judge [the] living and [the] dead, and [by] the appearing of him and the kingdom of him:
pieces: I solemnly charge you in the presence of God and of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, who will judge the living and the dead, and in view of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom:

L.1: I solemnly charge [you] before God and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, who is going to judge the living and the dead, and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom:

R.1: God and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus are watching. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} Jesus will judge everyone, both those who are alive and those who have died. He is coming back, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rule as king. So I give you this serious command:

decisions.choice: and by his appearing and his kingdom
decisions.reason: The accusatives are the things by which Paul makes the charge, as one swears by something; his return and reign are the reason to take it seriously.
In 1:10 ἐπιφάνειαν was his first coming; here, beside judgment and kingdom, it is his return.
Title setting.

decisions.choice: God and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus are watching
decisions.reason: Readable states what "before God" means.

records.heading: Preach the word

records.source: κήρυξον τὸν λόγον, ἐπίστηθι εὐκαίρως ἀκαίρως, ἔλεγξον, ἐπιτίμησον, παρακάλεσον, ἐν πάσῃ μακροθυμίᾳ καὶ διδαχῇ.
records.gloss: Preach the word, be ready in season [and] out of season, reprove, rebuke, exhort, with all patience and teaching.
pieces: Preach the word. Be ready whether the time seems right or not. Correct, rebuke and encourage, with great patience and careful teaching.

L.2: Preach the word; be ready in season [and] out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort, with complete patience and teaching.

R.2: Tell people God's message. Be ready to do it at all times, whether it is easy or hard. Show people what they are doing wrong. Warn them, and encourage them. Be very patient with them as you teach them.

decisions.choice: in season and out of season: whether convenient or not
decisions.reason: εὐκαίρως and ἀκαίρως are a play on words: when the moment is right and when it is not.

decisions.choice: the word: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: As in 2:9 and 2:15.

records.source: ἔσται γὰρ καιρὸς ὅτε τῆς ὑγιαινούσης διδασκαλίας οὐκ ἀνέξονται, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὰς ἰδίας ἐπιθυμίας ἑαυτοῖς ἐπισωρεύσουσιν διδασκάλους κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν, καὶ ἀπὸ μὲν τῆς ἀληθείας τὴν ἀκοὴν ἀποστρέψουσιν, ἐπὶ δὲ τοὺς μύθους ἐκτραπήσονται.
records.gloss: There will be for a time when the sound teaching not they will endure, but according to their own desires for themselves they will heap up teachers having itching the ear, \v 4 and from the truth the hearing they will turn away, to and the myths they will be turned aside.
pieces: For a time will come when people will not put up with sound teaching. Instead, wanting to hear what their ears itch for, they will gather around them a great number of teachers to suit their own desires.
They will turn away from listening to the truth and wander off into myths.

L.3: For the time will come when they will not put up with sound teaching, but, having itching ears, they will gather around themselves teachers to suit their own desires,
L.4: and they will turn their ears away from the truth and turn aside to myths.

R.3: A time will come when people will not want to listen to the true teaching. They will find many teachers who will tell them only what they want to hear, because they want to do whatever they like.
R.4: They will stop listening to the truth, and they will start to believe stories that people have made up.

decisions.choice: itching ears: wanting to hear something pleasing
decisions.reason: κνηθόμενοι is to have an itch: they want their ears tickled with what they like to hear.

decisions.choice: heap up: gather a great number
decisions.reason: ἐπισωρεύω is to pile up: they collect teacher after teacher.
As in 1 Timothy 1:4 and 4:7.

records.source: σὺ δὲ νῆφε ἐν πᾶσιν, κακοπάθησον, ἔργον ποίησον εὐαγγελιστοῦ, τὴν διακονίαν σου πληροφόρησον.
records.gloss: You but be sober in all things, suffer hardship, [the] work do of an evangelist, the ministry of you fully carry out.
pieces: But you, keep a clear head in every situation. Endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and carry out your ministry fully.

L.5: But as for you, be sober-minded in all things, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, fulfill your ministry.

R.5: But you must think clearly at all times. Be ready to suffer. Keep telling people the good news. Do everything God has given you to do.

decisions.choice: be sober-minded: be clear-headed and watchful
decisions.reason: νήφω is literally to be sober; here, to keep a clear mind, unlike those carried away by myths (verse 4).

decisions.choice: an evangelist: one who proclaims the good news
decisions.reason: εὐαγγελιστοῦ is one who brings the gospel to others (Acts 21:8; Ephesians 4:11).

decisions.choice: Keep telling people the good news
alternatives: do the work of an evangelist
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title (m2).

records.source: Ἐγὼ γὰρ ἤδη σπένδομαι, καὶ ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ἀναλύσεώς μου ἐφέστηκεν.
records.gloss: I for already am being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of the departure of me has come.
pieces: For I am already being poured out like a drink offering, and the time for my departure has come.

L.6: For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and the time of my departure has come.

R.6: My life is already being poured out like an offering to God. The time has come for me to leave this life.

decisions.choice: poured out as a drink offering
decisions.reason: σπένδομαι is to pour out a drink offering of wine, which accompanied sacrifices (Numbers 15:1-10). Paul sees his coming death as an offering to God (Philippians 2:17).
ἀναλύσεώς is the loosing of a ship from its moorings or the striking of a tent: leaving this life.
Readable makes clear that Paul means his death (m2).

records.heading: I have finished the race

records.source: τὸν καλὸν ἀγῶνα ἠγώνισμαι, τὸν δρόμον τετέλεκα, τὴν πίστιν τετήρηκα·
records.gloss: The good fight I have fought, the race I have finished, the faith I have kept;
pieces: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

L.7: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.

R.7: I have struggled hard in the contest, like an athlete. I have run the whole race. I have kept my faith.

decisions.choice: the good fight: the athlete's contest
decisions.reason: ἀγῶνα is any contest, especially in the games, as is the race that follows; compare 1 Timothy 6:12.

decisions.choice: kept the faith: stayed faithful, guarded the truth
alternatives: kept faith, as one keeps a promise
decisions.reason: τὴν πίστιν may be the Christian faith guarded (1:14) or Paul's own loyalty, as one keeps faith with a promise. Both are true of Paul.

decisions.choice: struggled hard in the contest, like an athlete
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture (m1).

records.source: λοιπὸν ἀπόκειταί μοι ὁ τῆς δικαιοσύνης στέφανος, ὃν ἀποδώσει μοι ὁ κύριος ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ, ὁ δίκαιος κριτής, οὐ μόνον δὲ ἐμοὶ ἀλλὰ καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἠγαπηκόσι τὴν ἐπιφάνειαν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: from now on is laid up for me the of righteousness crown, which will award to me the Lord in that day, the righteous judge, not only but to me but also to all those having loved the appearing of him.
pieces: Now there is waiting for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day, and not only to me but also to all who have longed for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing.

L.8: Henceforth the crown of righteousness is laid up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day, and not only to me but also to all who have loved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} appearing.

R.8: Now there is a prize waiting for me, the crown of righteousness. The Lord is a righteous judge, and on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes back {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give me this prize. He will give it not only to me but to everyone who has looked forward with love to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming.

decisions.choice: the crown of righteousness: the crown that is righteousness, or that rewards it
alternatives: the crown given to the righteous
decisions.reason: The genitive may mean the crown which consists of righteousness (final vindication) or the reward for a righteous life. Both fit the picture of the righteous judge.
στέφανος is the wreath given to the winner of a contest (2:5), not a royal crown.
Those who "love his appearing" are those who long for his return.

records.source: Σπούδασον ἐλθεῖν πρός με ταχέως·
records.gloss: Make every effort to come to me quickly;
pieces: Do your best to come to me soon.

L.9: Do your best to come to me quickly.

R.9: Try hard to come to me soon.

decisions.reason: σπουδάζω is to make haste, to be eager, as in 2:15 and 4:21.

records.heading: Come to me soon

records.source: Δημᾶς γάρ με ἐγκατέλιπεν ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα, καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην, Κρήσκης εἰς Γαλατίαν, Τίτος εἰς Δαλματίαν·
records.gloss: Demas for me has deserted, having loved the present age, and has gone to Thessalonica, Crescens to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia;
pieces: Demas, in love with this present world, has deserted me and gone to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia and Titus to Dalmatia.

L.10: For Demas has deserted me, having loved the present age, and has gone to Thessalonica; Crescens [has gone] to Galatia, Titus to Dalmatia.

R.10: Demas loved the things of this world too much, so he left me and went to Thessalonica. Crescens has gone to Galatia, and Titus has gone to Dalmatia.

decisions.reason: Demas was with Paul in his earlier imprisonment (Colossians 4:14; Philemon 24).

decisions.choice: the present age: this world and its life
decisions.reason: αἰῶνα is an age; "the present age" is the world as it now is, set against the coming one.
Galatia was in central Asia Minor (some manuscripts read "Gaul"); Dalmatia is on the eastern Adriatic coast (modern Croatia). Crescens and Titus seem to have gone on mission, not deserted.
The sense is this world and its life (m2).

records.source: Λουκᾶς ἐστιν μόνος μετ’ ἐμοῦ.
records.gloss: Luke is alone with me.
pieces: Only Luke is with me.

R.11: Only Luke is with me now.

decisions.reason: Luke, "the beloved physician" (Colossians 4:14), traveled with Paul (Acts 16:10, 27:1).

records.source: Μᾶρκον ἀναλαβὼν ἄγε μετὰ σεαυτοῦ, ἔστιν γάρ μοι εὔχρηστος εἰς διακονίαν, Τυχικὸν δὲ ἀπέστειλα εἰς Ἔφεσον.
records.gloss: Mark having taken bring with yourself, he is for to me useful for ministry. \v 12 Tychicus but I sent to Ephesus.
pieces: Get Mark and bring him with you, because he is helpful to me in my work.
I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.

L.11: Get Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me for ministry.
L.12: But Tychicus I have sent to Ephesus.

R.11: Find Mark and bring him with you. He can help me in my work.
R.12: I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.

decisions.choice: Mark: once a cause of division, now useful
decisions.reason: John Mark left Paul on his first journey, and Paul refused to take him again (Acts 13:13, 15:37-39). Later Mark was with Paul again (Colossians 4:10; Philemon 24).

decisions.choice: ministry: service, either to Paul or in the gospel
decisions.reason: διακονίαν may be personal help to Paul or service in the work of the gospel.
Tychicus was Paul's trusted messenger (Ephesians 6:21; Colossians 4:7). He may have carried this letter, and replaced Timothy in Ephesus.

records.source: τὸν φαιλόνην, ὃν ἀπέλιπον ἐν Τρῳάδι παρὰ Κάρπῳ, ἐρχόμενος φέρε, καὶ τὰ βιβλία, μάλιστα τὰς μεμβράνας.
records.gloss: The cloak which I left in Troas with Carpus, coming bring, and the books, especially the parchments.
pieces: When you come, bring the cloak I left with Carpus at Troas, and my scrolls, especially the parchments.

L.13: When you come, bring the cloak that I left in Troas with Carpus, and the books, especially the parchments.

R.13: When you come, bring the coat that I left with Carpus in Troas. Also bring my books, especially the ones written on parchment.

decisions.choice: the cloak: a heavy outer garment
decisions.reason: φαιλόνην is a heavy, sleeveless cape, needed in a prison as winter came (verse 21).
βιβλία are scrolls, probably papyrus. μεμβράνας are sheets of parchment (prepared animal skin), perhaps notebooks or copies of the Scriptures. We do not know their contents.

records.source: Ἀλέξανδρος ὁ χαλκεὺς πολλά μοι κακὰ ἐνεδείξατο ἀποδώσει αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος κατὰ τὰ ἔργα αὐτοῦ ὃν καὶ σὺ φυλάσσου, λίαν γὰρ ἀντέστη τοῖς ἡμετέροις λόγοις.
records.gloss: Alexander the coppersmith many to me evils did; will repay him the Lord according to the deeds of him; \v 15 whom also you guard against, greatly for he opposed our words.
pieces: Alexander the metalworker did me a great deal of harm. The Lord will repay him for what he has done.
You too should be on guard against him, because he strongly opposed our message.

L.14: Alexander the coppersmith did me much harm; the Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
L.15: You also beware of him, for he strongly opposed our words.

R.14: Alexander, who works with metal, did many bad things to me. The Lord will punish him for what he has done.
R.15: You must be careful of him too, because he fought hard against what we teach.

decisions.reason: Perhaps the Alexander of 1 Timothy 1:20, or of Acts 19:33; the name was common. χαλκεὺς is a smith in copper or bronze, or any metalworker.

decisions.choice: the Lord will repay him according to his deeds
decisions.reason: The words echo Psalm 62:13 and Proverbs 24:12. Some manuscripts have the wish "may the Lord repay"; the SBLGNT has the future.
λόγοις is plural: Paul's preaching, or his defense at his trial.

records.source: Ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ μου ἀπολογίᾳ οὐδείς μοι παρεγένετο, ἀλλὰ πάντες με ἐγκατέλιπον μὴ αὐτοῖς λογισθείη ὁ δὲ κύριός μοι παρέστη καὶ ἐνεδυνάμωσέν με, ἵνα δι’ ἐμοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα πληροφορηθῇ καὶ ἀκούσωσιν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἐρρύσθην ἐκ στόματος λέοντος.
records.gloss: At the first of me defense no one me stood by, but all me deserted; not to them may it be counted; \v 17 the but Lord me stood by and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully carried out and might hear all the Gentiles, and I was rescued out of [the] mouth of a lion.
pieces: At my first defense no one came to support me; everyone deserted me. May it not be held against them.
But the Lord stood by me and gave me strength, so that through me the message might be fully proclaimed and all the Gentiles might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion's mouth.

L.16: At my first defense no one stood by me, but all deserted me. May it not be counted against them.
L.17: But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be fully carried out and all the Gentiles might hear [it]; and I was rescued from the lion's mouth.

R.16: The first time I had to defend myself in court, no one came to help me. They all left me alone. I pray that God will not hold it against them.
R.17: But the Lord stayed with me and made me strong. He did this so that I could tell the whole message, and all the Gentiles could hear it. And the Lord saved me from great danger, as if from the mouth of a lion.

decisions.choice: my first defense: the first hearing of Paul's trial
alternatives: his defense at an earlier imprisonment
decisions.reason: A Roman trial could have a preliminary hearing. Paul speaks of it as recent, so it is probably the first stage of his present trial.
The phrase recalls Psalm 22:22 and Daniel 6. It is a picture of mortal danger; some have seen a reference to Nero or to the arena, but as a Roman citizen Paul would not be thrown to the lions.

decisions.choice: may it not be counted against them
decisions.reason: Like Jesus (Luke 23:34) and Stephen (Acts 7:60), Paul forgives those who failed him.

decisions.choice: saved me from great danger, as if from the mouth of a lion
decisions.reason: Readable states the picture (m2).

records.heading: The Lord stood by me

records.source: ῥύσεταί με ὁ κύριος ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔργου πονηροῦ καὶ σώσει εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ τὴν ἐπουράνιον· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
records.gloss: Will rescue me the Lord from every work evil and will save into the kingdom of him the heavenly; to whom [be] the glory to the ages of the ages, amen.
pieces: The Lord will rescue me from every evil attack and bring me safely into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heavenly kingdom. To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

L.18: The Lord will rescue me from every evil deed and will bring [me] safely into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} heavenly kingdom. To {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [be] the glory for ever and ever. Amen.

R.18: The Lord will save me from every evil thing that people try to do to me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bring me safely into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom in heaven. Give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory for ever and ever. Amen.

decisions.choice: will bring me safely into his kingdom
decisions.reason: σώσει is the verb "save", here meaning to bring safe through to the end. Paul does not expect rescue from death (verse 6) but rescue through it.
Literally "to the ages of the ages", an idiom for eternity.

decisions.choice: bring [me] safely (L); bring me safely (B, R)
decisions.reason: The sense is safe arrival (m1), so the key term "save" is not used for this word.

records.source: Ἄσπασαι Πρίσκαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν καὶ τὸν Ὀνησιφόρου οἶκον.
records.gloss: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the of Onesiphorus household.
pieces: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.

L.19: Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.

R.19: Say hello to Prisca and Aquila and to the family of Onesiphorus.

decisions.reason: A married couple, tentmakers like Paul, who worked with him in Corinth and Ephesus (Acts 18:2-3, 18:26). Prisca is the Priscilla of Acts; she is often named first.

records.heading: Final greetings

records.source: Ἔραστος ἔμεινεν ἐν Κορίνθῳ, Τρόφιμον δὲ ἀπέλιπον ἐν Μιλήτῳ ἀσθενοῦντα.
records.gloss: Erastus remained in Corinth, Trophimus but I left in Miletus being sick.
pieces: Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.

L.20: Erastus remained in Corinth, but Trophimus I left sick in Miletus.

R.20: Erastus stayed in Corinth. Trophimus was sick, so I left him in Miletus.

decisions.reason: Erastus may be the city official of Corinth (Romans 16:23) or Paul's helper (Acts 19:22). Trophimus was from Ephesus (Acts 20:4, 21:29). Miletus is a port south of Ephesus.

records.source: Σπούδασον πρὸ χειμῶνος ἐλθεῖν.
records.gloss: Make every effort before winter to come.
pieces: Do your best to get here before winter.

L.21: Do your best to come before winter.

R.21: Try hard to come before winter.

decisions.reason: Ships stopped sailing in winter (Acts 27:9-12); if Timothy waited, he could not come until spring.

records.source: Ἀσπάζεταί σε Εὔβουλος καὶ Πούδης καὶ Λίνος καὶ Κλαυδία καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες.
records.gloss: Greets you Eubulus and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and the brothers all.
pieces: Eubulus sends you greetings, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

L.21: Eubulus greets you, and Pudens and Linus and Claudia and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.

R.21: Eubulus says hello to you. So do Pudens, Linus, Claudia and all the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} here.

decisions.reason: Believers in Rome; Claudia is a woman. Irenaeus names a Linus as an early leader of the church in Rome.

decisions.choice: the brothers: fellow believers, men and women
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοὶ was used for all believers in a church.
The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

records.source: Ὁ κύριος μετὰ τοῦ πνεύματός σου.
records.gloss: The Lord [be] with the spirit of you.
pieces: The Lord be with your spirit.

R.22: I pray that the Lord will be with you.

decisions.reason: σου is singular; the final blessing (s2) is plural.
Many manuscripts read "the Lord Jesus Christ" or "the Lord Jesus".

records.source: ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν.
records.gloss: The grace [be] with you all.
pieces: Grace be with you all.

R.22: I pray that God will show grace to all of you.

decisions.choice: you: plural, to the church with Timothy
decisions.reason: ὑμῶν is plural: the letter is personal, but read in the church.
Many manuscripts add "Amen".
English "you" does not show the plural (m1).
